# Watch commands

> **Always bound a watch**: pass `--frames <N>` and/or `--max-ms <MS>` or the stream runs until the pipe closes. Frames print as JSONL. The 60 s budget ceiling applies to the MCP watch tools only, not to these subcommands.

## brp watch get-components

Watch a specific entity's components, streaming each frame as JSONL

```text
Watch a specific entity's components, streaming each frame as JSONL

Usage: bevy_copilot brp watch get-components [OPTIONS] <ENTITY>

Arguments:
  <ENTITY>  Entity ID to watch

Options:
      --components <COMPONENTS>  Component type paths to watch
      --host <HOST>              Host of the BRP HTTP endpoint (env BEVY_BRP_HOST, default 127.0.0.1)
      --frames <FRAMES>          Maximum number of frames to collect
      --port <PORT>              Port of the BRP HTTP endpoint (env BEVY_BRP_PORT, default 15702)
      --compact <COMPACT>        Compact (single-line) JSON output instead of pretty: true|false [possible values: true, false]
      --max-ms <MAX_MS>          Time budget in milliseconds (unclamped on the CLI; the 60s ceiling applies to MCP watch tools only)
      --skip-first <SKIP_FIRST>  Skip the first frame of the stream: true|false [possible values: true, false]
  -h, --help                     Print help
```

MCP peer: `brp_get_components_watch`

## brp watch list-components

Watch component list changes for one entity or the world, streaming JSONL

```text
Watch component list changes for one entity or the world, streaming JSONL

Usage: bevy_copilot brp watch list-components [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --entity <ENTITY>          Entity ID to watch (omit for the whole world)
```

## brp watch observe

Watch an entity via world.observe, streaming each frame as JSONL

```text
Watch an entity via world.observe, streaming each frame as JSONL

Usage: bevy_copilot brp watch observe [OPTIONS] --event <EVENT>

Options:
      --entity <ENTITY>          Entity ID to observe (optional, defaults to world.observe behavior)
      --host <HOST>              Host of the BRP HTTP endpoint (env BEVY_BRP_HOST, default 127.0.0.1)
      --event <EVENT>            Observe event label
      --port <PORT>              Port of the BRP HTTP endpoint (env BEVY_BRP_PORT, default 15702)
      --compact <COMPACT>        Compact (single-line) JSON output instead of pretty: true|false [possible values: true, false]
      --frames <FRAMES>          Maximum number of frames to collect
      --max-ms <MAX_MS>          Time budget in milliseconds (unclamped on the CLI; the 60s ceiling applies to MCP watch tools only)
      --skip-first <SKIP_FIRST>  Skip the first frame of the stream: true|false [possible values: true, false]
  -h, --help                     Print help
```

MCP peer: `brp_observe_watch`
